THE STORY // WHY BUILD THE PROOF?

I MISSED THE DOOR.
THE TRUST MODEL MISSED THE MOMENT.

I scored a 126 on the AMC 12 and an 11 on the AIME, producing a USAMO qualification index of 236. That score would have qualified in every earlier year. Instead, the COVID-disrupted competition cycle produced a record-high cutoff and left me just outside.

It was not just some random statistical fluke. The cutoff spike arrived during COVID-era testing, amid alleged reports of AI-assisted test-taking. That made a bigger problem impossible to ignore: an assessment built around what a student can see and write can no longer assume those are the only systems in the room.

I built CheatGPT as a visible proof of concept—not to take a test for me, but to show how little friction now separates a camera, an inference model, and a private display. The demonstration above is deliberately staged and pre-recorded. It exposes the capability without publishing a covert cheating playbook.

For the record: I do not even wear glasses. Consider that my least technical—and most literal—way of saying I do not condone using them to cheat.

THESIS // 001
“When inference becomes ambient, integrity has to be designed—not assumed.”

Better assessments can emphasize oral defense, process artifacts, unique data, and teacher-visible iteration—not an arms race of surveillance.

THE REDIRECT // SAME PIPELINE, BETTER PURPOSE

REAL-TIME INFERENCE
CAN STILL DO GOOD.

Camera → context → inference → display is morally neutral. The product choices around consent, timing, and what the system returns are what redirect it.

01 // ACCESS

See what others hear.

Live captions, translation, sign reading, object cues, and navigation prompts for people with hearing or visual impairments.

RETURN: CONTEXT, NOT CONTROL
02 // LEARN

Coach without answering.

A Socratic tutor can detect the step where reasoning breaks, offer one hint, and reserve full solutions for post-attempt review.

RETURN: THE NEXT QUESTION
03 // BUILD

Keep hands on the work.

Technicians, nurses, and makers can see checklists, diagrams, and verified procedures while both hands stay on the task.

RETURN: VERIFIED GUIDANCE
04 // PROTECT

Catch the missed step.

Consent-based prompts can flag a skipped safety check, a medication mismatch, or an equipment state that deserves a second look.

RETURN: A PAUSE, NOT A VERDICT
DESIGN RULE

A constructive version should be visible, consent-based, auditable, and easy to pause. It should preserve human agency and withhold outputs when the context makes assistance inappropriate.
